sovereign_country.strategic_role: 连接拉美市场的欧洲商贸桥梁、本地化仓配与数字游民签证

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Merchant Acquiring and Clearing Service Provider (PSP)

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Active Spanish bilateral investment treaties (APPRI) with Latin American counterparts
Active Spanish double taxation agreements with Spain–United States, Spain–Mexico, Spain–Chile and Spain–Colombia
EU Free Trade Agreements with Mexico, Chile and Colombia, as in force, relevant to payment services

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto 10/2021, de 25 de mayo, por el que se crea y regula el Registro Central de Titularidad Real; supplemented by EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843 as transposed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of certificate of incorporation and corporate registry documents for any corporate shareholder/UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial/Companies Registry in the jurisdiction of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the issuer is outside the Hague Convention, consular legalization through the competent Spanish consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Poder) authorizing the Spanish incorporation representative and notary filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of record in the jurisdiction of the grantor

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copies of the passport/ID of all directors, shareholders, UBOs and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the jurisdiction where each person is present

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / current status certificate for all corporate investors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry/Chamber of Commerce in the corporate investor's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds confirmation for the investment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature or SWIFT-confirmed banker's letter; apostille/consular legalization when the Spanish notary requires it

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Under Ley 10/2010 arts. 3, 4, 6 and 14, all UBOs, directors, shareholders and authorized signatories must be screened before notarial execution against: UN Security Council consolidated list; EU consolidated financial sanctions list (EUDOF); OFAC SDN, SSI and Non-SDN lists; SEPBLAC/Bank of Spain internal warning lists; and reputable international PEP databases. Any match requires immediate enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, and SEPBLAC reporting. A negative screening result is a precondition to proceeding with the PSP license application.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) online negative name certification – Sede Electrónica del Registro Mercantil Central (https://www.rmc.es)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Roman script; Spanish and Spain's co-official languages are admissible. Any name in a non-Latin script must be transliterated into Spanish/Latin characters before submission. The registered name must not be identical, phonetically indistinguishable, or misleadingly similar to an existing Spanish company name, per art. 8 of Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RMC negative name certificate and reservation are valid for 90 days and may be extended once for an equal period. Upon rejection, the applicant may file an optional recurso de reposición with the RMC within one month, followed by a recurso de alzada before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (Ministry of Justice) within one month. A judicial appeal before the competent Madrid administrative court is available within two months. Re-filing of a new name application and payment of the applicable fee are required for any substitute name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a standard SL, a virtual office is acceptable only as a correspondence address; the statutory domicile must be a physical location in Spain where central administration or the principal establishment is situated, per art. 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital. For a licensed payment institution under the Spanish transposition of PSD2, a virtual office is impermissible: a tangible physical office, local management, and auditable compliance infrastructure in Spain are mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Pre-incorporation address verification by the Registro Mercantil is low (<10%) absent red flags. Post-licence supervision by the Bank of Spain is high: approximately 80–90% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 18 months of operations, consistent with the High_Risk_Special_License classification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice/Ministry of Foreign Affairs and consulates, plus sworn translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for legalization and sworn translation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarized Power of Attorney for incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary in the grantor's jurisdiction and Spanish consular/legalization office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff plus market benchmark for apostille processing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of incorporation deed and bylaws (escritura de constitución and estatutos)
Notary public fee for execution of the incorporation deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish notary (Colegio Notarial of the incorporation province)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provisional Spanish tax number (NIF provisional) application coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AEAT (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria) plus incorporating counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for representation; AEAT itself charges no filing fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Central Beneficial Ownership Registry / SEPBLAC compliance channel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for compliance preparation and filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT pre-incorporation screening and risk assessment (UBO, PEP and sanctions)
Pre-incorporation regulatory readiness assessment for PSP license (Bank of Spain / PSD2)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital, Articles 20, 22, 30, and 62.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (for name certification) and the relevant Registro Mercantil Provincial (for inscription of the company in the commercial registry).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de constitución otorgada ante notario, filed with the Registro Mercantil Provincial.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 3,000 minimum share capital, fully subscribed and paid-up in cash at incorporation. The funds must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution and the resulting blocking certificate is required before the notarial deed is executed; the block is released upon registration in the Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share subscription be ratified. All shares have been fully subscribed and paid in cash pursuant to Article 62 of the Spanish Capital Companies Act. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at Calle de Madrid, 1, Madrid, Spain, as stated in the deed of incorporation, and that registration in the Mercantile Registry be pursued. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Sole Administrator and [Name] Secretary, with power to open bank accounts, obtain the provisional tax identification number, execute notarial filings, and apply for the payment institution license. RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to take all ancillary steps.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Madrid, through its electronic office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application to the Registro Mercantil Central proposing up to three alternative company names. The Registry checks the proposed names against the official corporate-name index and issues a certificate confirming that the selected name has not been previously registered and is admissible.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity document of the founding member or legal representative
List of three preferred company names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused because of identity with an existing company or inadmissibility, resubmit the application with alternative names or file a written challenge before the commercial registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening a temporary capital-deposit bank account and obtaining the blocking certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution lawfully operating in Spain.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company in formation and deposit the statutory minimum capital of EUR 3,000. Instruct the bank to issue a blocking certificate stating that the funds are deposited and subject to the company's incorporation, to be released only upon registration in the Commercial Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional compliance information, supply corrected constitutional documents, clarify beneficial ownership, or select another credit institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary Public (Notario) in the jurisdiction of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary with the preliminary name certificate, bank blocking certificate, statutory articles, and identity documents. The notary verifies legal capacity, capital payment, and legality of the deed, then executes the public deed of incorporation and issues the original and certified copies.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association signed by all founding members
Passport or NIE of each founding member
Power of attorney for any representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary reports defects, rectify the deed through an addendum or a private corrective document, then re-execute the deed before the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the provisional tax identification number (NIF provisional) from the tax authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), territorial office or electronic register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the tax census declaration on Form 036 along with a certified copy of the notarial deed of incorporation. The AEAT assigns the provisional NIF, which remains valid until final registration and issuance of the definitive NIF.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or queried, correct the Form 036, provide missing identification, or resubmit with a Spanish translation or apostilled documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office, Madrid.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the first copy of the notarial deed, together with the provisional NIF certificate, at the Commercial Registry. The registrar examines the legality of the deed, statutory provisions, and shareholder appointments, and subsequently records the company, after which the definitive NIF is obtained and the company becomes validly incorporated with legal personality.
required_dossiers: First copy of the notarial deed of incorporation
Bank statement evidencing deposit and blocking
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a note of defects or suspension, cure the reservations by means of a corrective notarial deed, supplemental clarification, or formal appeal to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Banco de España – Dirección General de Supervisión, authorizing body for payment institutions; municipal council (Ayuntamiento) with competence for the activity/opening license and administrative environmental clearance for the office premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorización administrativa previa como entidad de pago (payment institution license under Law 21/2007, as amended by Royal Decree-Law 19/2018 and PSD2).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD), Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental, together with the competent municipal environmental body
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No full EIA report required for a payment gateway/office operation; classed as low-impact professional activity requiring only municipal environmental registration or, at most, a simplified environmental assessment (evaluación ambiental simplificada).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the general air quality/emission limits under Royal Decree 102/2011 where emergency generators are installed; wastewater discharges to municipal sewers must meet local sewer ordinance limits; waste electrical and electronic equipment must be handled under Royal Decree 110/2015; no material VOC emissions expected absent industrial processing; UPS/battery rooms must conform to applicable chemical storage and spill-control rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Technical Building Code Basic Document SI (Seguridad en caso de incendio); municipal activity license or responsible declaration for the office premises; occupational risk prevention plan and workplace health and safety assessment; structural load verification for IT and server equipment; electrical installation and lightning protection inspection; emergency evacuation plan and civil defense clearance in accordance with local fire brigade requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT. Spanish tax identification numbers are administered through the Registro de Operadores Económicos and the census of taxpayers. Regional tax authorities generally do not administer ordinary national corporate income tax or VAT registration for entities established in Spain.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) by filing Modelo 036 with the AEAT. A provisional NIF may be requested after execution of the incorporation deed and before registration with the Mercantile Registry; the definitive NIF must be obtained after registration by submitting the registered deed and updated corporate information within the applicable filing period. The NIF normally uses the Spanish legal-entity format beginning with the letter B for an ordinary Spanish limited liability company. A foreign entity without a Spanish establishment obtains an NIF through Modelo 036, directly or through an authorized representative, providing constitutional documents, evidence of legal existence, registered address, identification of directors or legal representatives, and proof of authority. Foreign documents may require apostille or legalization and an official Spanish translation. VAT registration is generally performed through the same census filing. An entity carrying out intra-Community transactions should apply for inclusion in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and obtain a VAT number activated for VIES purposes. A Spanish VAT number is generally the NIF prefixed by ES. Additional registrations may be required for the Immediate Supply of Information system (SII), the monthly VAT refund register (REDEME), or other sectoral tax obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no general United States-style check-the-box election for a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. The SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal taxpayer. Available elections or optional regimes may include tax consolidation for qualifying corporate groups, the special regime for mergers and other corporate reorganizations, the special regime for entities engaged in leasing housing, the VAT cash-accounting regime where eligibility conditions are met, and certain investment or holding-company regimes. A Spanish SL is not ordinarily eligible to elect transparent treatment merely by filing an election. Spanish anti-hybrid mismatch rules may deny deductions, impose inclusion, or otherwise neutralize mismatches involving hybrid entities, instruments, or imported arrangements. The payment-services activity may also require authorization or registration as a payment institution, electronic-money institution, or other regulated provider under Spanish and European payment-services legislation; tax registration does not substitute for financial-regulatory authorization.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA), governed principally by Law 37/1992 and related regulations. Spanish VAT applies in mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands. The Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla are outside the territorial scope of Spanish VAT and have separate indirect-tax systems.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 for ordinary domestic taxable activity: Spain generally has no general turnover threshold below which an established business is automatically exempt from VAT registration. A person carrying out an independent economic activity must register in the taxpayer census before commencing taxable activity, subject to applicable place-of-supply rules and exemptions. A separate EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold applies to certain intra-Community distance sales and electronically supplied, telecommunications, broadcasting, and similar services supplied to EU consumers, unless the supplier opts for destination taxation or uses the One Stop Shop. The threshold is not a general Spanish VAT-registration exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time pre-clearance system for every VAT invoice. Taxpayers within the mandatory SII regime, including qualifying large businesses with turnover exceeding EUR 6 million, VAT groups, REDEME entities, and voluntary participants, must transmit specified VAT ledger information electronically to the AEAT, generally within four calendar days, excluding certain holiday adjustments. Electronic invoicing and invoice-content rules are governed principally by Spanish invoicing legislation, including Royal Decree 1619/2012. Certified billing systems must preserve integrity, traceability, accessibility, legibility, and anti-tampering controls under the applicable requirements introduced by Law 11/2021 and Royal Decree 1007/2023, with implementation dates subject to subsequent regulatory amendments. The forthcoming B2B electronic-invoicing framework under the Create and Grow Law requires technical and procedural implementation before becoming generally operative. A payment gateway should maintain invoice, transaction, settlement, merchant, customer-location, chargeback, refund, and VAT-rate evidence capable of supporting place-of-supply and audit controls.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from the Spanish VAT territory to destinations outside the European Union may qualify for the 0% VAT exemption with a right to deduct input VAT where the supplier or an authorized customer transports or dispatches the goods outside the EU and the export is substantiated by customs evidence and proof of exit. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for exemption where the customer is identified for VAT in another EU Member State, the goods are dispatched to that Member State, the supplier reports the transaction correctly, and transport and customer-status evidence are retained. Services supplied to business customers established outside the EU may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT under the business-customer place-of-supply rule, subject to use-and-enjoyment restrictions and special rules for services connected with immovable property, events, transport, telecommunications, financial services, and other categories. Financial and payment services may also be VAT-exempt under specific statutory provisions, but exemption classification must be determined transaction by transaction; a payment gateway is not automatically entitled to treat all processing, technical, platform, or ancillary services as exempt. Export treatment requires contemporaneous evidence of customer status, contractual scope, payment flows, destination, transport or use, and the applicable place-of-supply rule.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration filed through the Spanish customs system, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Commercial invoice and contract or order documentation identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, and delivery terms
Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note, courier record, or equivalent logistics evidence
Customs exit confirmation or equivalent electronic proof that the goods physically left the EU customs territory
Packing list and, where relevant, export licenses, permits, certificates of origin, and product-specific regulatory documents
Evidence of the purchaser's non-EU establishment or VAT status where relevant to the exemption
Accounting records, VAT ledgers, payment and settlement records, and reconciliation between invoice, customs declaration, and receipt

For offshore services: contract, customer tax-residence or business-status evidence, service-delivery records, platform or usage logs where relevant, and evidence supporting the applicable place-of-supply rule
Inward remittance evidence may support commercial and audit substantiation but is not generally a universal statutory condition for Spanish VAT export exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general foreign-exchange rule requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days. Export proceeds may remain abroad subject to ordinary accounting, anti-money-laundering, payment-services, transfer-pricing, financial-reporting, and beneficial-ownership requirements. If a zero-rating or exemption is unsupported, the AEAT may assess output VAT retrospectively, deny or claw back input-VAT recovery, impose late-payment interest, and apply penalties under the General Tax Law 58/2003 and VAT Law 37/1992. Tax penalties for inaccurate or fraudulent tax treatment commonly range from 50% to 150% of the improperly avoided or unduly refunded tax, depending on the statutory classification, with aggravation for concealment, fraudulent means, or repeated conduct. False customs declarations may trigger customs debt, recovery of duties and taxes, customs penalties, and seizure or other measures under the Union Customs Code and Spanish implementing rules. Material intentional VAT fraud may also create criminal exposure under the Spanish Criminal Code, including liability where the defrauded tax quota exceeds the applicable criminal threshold. Refunds obtained without entitlement are recoverable with interest, and repeated unsupported export claims may result in heightened audit, denial of refund procedures, and referral to customs, financial-intelligence, or payment-services regulators.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: European Central Bank and Banco de España, with anti-money-laundering supervision and suspicious-transaction reporting administered by the Executive Service of the Commission for the Prevention of Money Laundering and Monetary Offences (SEPBLAC). Payment institutions and electronic-money institutions are principally supervised by Banco de España under the Spanish transposition of the EU Payment Services and Electronic Money frameworks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and is subject to the EU single-market framework. The euro is fully convertible for ordinary current-account transactions, including trade payments, service fees, dividends, interest and other lawful remittances. Spain has no general exchange-control approval requirement for ordinary inbound or outbound payments. Capital-account transactions, shareholder loans, intercompany financing, acquisitions and disposals are generally permitted but may trigger statistical, foreign-investment, tax, beneficial-ownership, anti-money-laundering or sector-specific reporting. Profit remittance normally requires distributable accounting profits, approval of annual accounts and the distribution resolution, satisfaction of legal-reserve requirements, solvent payment capacity, proper withholding-tax analysis and maintenance of supporting books and records. Payments involving sanctioned parties, opaque ownership, unusual payment chains, unlicensed payment activity or inadequate source-of-funds evidence may be blocked or delayed by banks. A payment gateway must not confuse unrestricted euro convertibility with permission to provide regulated payment services without the required Banco de España authorization or passporting status.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Exporters may retain foreign-currency proceeds, subject to banking, accounting, tax, sanctions and anti-money-laundering controls. There is no general statutory deadline requiring conversion of export proceeds into euros. The company must retain commercial invoices, contracts, customs or delivery evidence where applicable, settlement records and reconciliation evidence. Banco de España statistical reporting may apply to relevant cross-border transactions or external liabilities under applicable reporting instructions and thresholds; these reporting obligations do not constitute a mandatory surrender or conversion rule. Physical cash or bearer negotiable instruments transported into or out of the EU at EUR 10,000 or more, or equivalent, are subject to EU cash-declaration requirements. Banks may impose contractual conversion, documentation or settlement requirements under their risk policies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operational payments and treasury diversification, but low as a substitute for a fully integrated Spanish banking relationship. An offshore digital EMI cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services to or from Spain solely because it offers an online account. The provider must be authorized in its home EEA state and validly passport services into Spain, or hold the relevant Spanish authorization. Customer funds must be safeguarded under the applicable payment-services or electronic-money regime and must not be used as ordinary corporate working capital. An EMI account may lack cash services, Spanish domestic lending, capital-escrow functionality, reliable correspondent access, card-scheme acquiring capability or support for high-risk merchant flows. A payment gateway operating merchant acquiring, payment initiation, money remittance, account-information, issuance or acquiring functions must map each activity to the applicable PSD2 authorization, electronic-money authorization, agent, outsourcing and safeguarding requirements. Direct Fedwire access is generally unavailable to an EU corporate or non-US EMI and normally requires a US correspondent or regulated payment partner.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement for every director to appear physically at a bank branch. Banks may permit remote onboarding using qualified electronic signatures, video identification, certified corporate documents and enhanced verification. In practice, a bank may require a live video interview, physical attendance by an authorized representative, notarized or apostilled documents, original-document review or a Spanish notarial process, particularly for non-resident directors, complex ownership, payment-service businesses, Latin American corridors, virtual offices, high transaction volumes or elevated sanctions and fraud risk. The company should obtain a Spanish tax identification number, register the SL, evidence its registered office and operating substance, identify all beneficial owners and provide a board or shareholder mandate for account operation. Remote onboarding is discretionary and cannot be assumed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The stated activity is online merchant acquiring, clearing or payment processing, but the applicant cannot demonstrate the applicable Banco de España authorization, EEA passport, regulated partner arrangement or clearly limited technology-services role.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authorization or passporting evidence; regulatory perimeter memorandum; business-flow diagram; funds-flow and safeguarding map; copies of regulated-partner agreements; outsourcing and sub-processing schedule; merchant-acquisition contracts; compliance officer appointment; AML and sanctions policies; transaction-monitoring methodology; complaints and safeguarding procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership, nominee shareholders, layered offshore ownership, bearer-style documentation or inconsistent ownership information across corporate records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents; current commercial-register extracts; ownership chart to natural-person beneficial owners; passports and residential-address evidence for directors, shareholders and UBOs; trust or foundation documents where applicable; notarized powers of attorney; written explanation of control rights; independent corporate-secretarial certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership and directors combined with a Spanish registered office but no credible local management, employees, technology, compliance function or operating rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan; Spanish office lease or service agreement with substance explanation; employment or contractor agreements; organization chart; board minutes; local compliance arrangements; technology architecture; projected transaction volumes; target-market analysis; customer and merchant onboarding policy; tax-residency and permanent-establishment analysis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-volume cross-border flows, rapid pass-through of funds, Latin American corridors, nested payment relationships or merchant activity involving high-risk sectors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country and corridor risk assessment; merchant underwriting standards; prohibited-business list; enhanced due-diligence policy; sample merchant files; transaction-monitoring scenarios; velocity and exposure limits; chargeback and fraud controls; sanctions-screening configuration; reconciliation reports; reserve policy; independent compliance testing plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming shareholder capital or intercompany funding does not match the capital structure, stated purpose or sender identity, or is routed through unrelated third parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital-increase or shareholder-loan agreement; board and shareholder resolutions; bank statements showing source of funds; audited or management accounts of the funder; tax-residency certificates; ownership evidence; beneficial-owner declarations; payment instruction identifying the legal purpose; Spanish accounting entries; related-party pricing analysis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected transaction volumes are inconsistent with the company’s incorporation stage, stated revenue model or declared source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year financial model; signed customer or merchant contracts; acquiring-bank or processor agreements; invoices; payment-volume forecast by country and currency; liquidity plan; capital adequacy and safeguarding calculations; explanation of seasonality; independent accountant confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse media, fraud, cybercrime or high-risk-country exposure involving owners, directors, merchants, payers, beneficiaries or correspondent institutions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Identity-resolution report; documented false-positive analysis; PEP and sanctions screening results; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; enhanced due-diligence approval; beneficial-owner declarations; contractual representations; escalation and exit criteria; evidence of ongoing monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, unregulated wallets, offshore virtual IBANs or unrelated third-party accounts for company receipts or merchant settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal treasury policy; approved account list; segregation-of-funds procedures; bank-account ownership evidence; reconciliation controls; payment approval matrix; regulated-provider contracts; written explanation of historical transactions; remediation plan and independent control sign-off.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete Spanish tax, corporate or beneficial-ownership records, including missing NIF, outdated commercial-register information or inconsistent registered-office details.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish NIF certificate; deed of incorporation; registered commercial-register extract; beneficial-ownership declaration; powers of attorney; tax registration evidence; registered-office proof; annual filing calendar; accountant or gestor certification; updated director and shareholder register.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through a bank account in the name of the Spanish SL using SEPA Credit Transfer for euro funding or SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA currencies. The remitter should be the shareholder, parent or documented lender identified in the corporate records; third-party funding should be avoided unless legally documented and pre-cleared. The payment reference should state the legal purpose, such as share-capital contribution, capital increase, shareholder loan or intercompany loan, and must identify the relevant agreement or resolution. For an incorporation or formal capital increase, obtain the bank’s capital-deposit certificate where required by the notary or registry process; after registration, transfer funds to the operating account under the bank’s instructions. For a shareholder loan, retain the executed agreement, maturity, interest, repayment terms, transfer-pricing support and beneficial-owner evidence. Provide source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation, sender and beneficiary tax identifiers, ownership records and expected-use information. There is no universal Spanish FX purpose-code regime equivalent to a mandatory conversion code for ordinary commercial wires; banks may nevertheless require internal purpose categories, LEI, invoice references, VAT data, counterparty details and supporting documents. Reconcile every inbound transfer to the general ledger and investigate rejected, returned or mismatched payments.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA scheme, subject to bank limits and sanctions screening. Use SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA commercial wires, with complete originator, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, purpose and Ultimate Beneficial Owner information. Use documentary commercial letters of credit issued or confirmed by a bank under UCP 600 where counterparty, country or performance risk justifies documentary settlement; align the invoice, transport documents, insurance, inspection certificate and beneficiary details precisely with the credit. Documentary collections may use URC 522 where appropriate but provide less payment certainty than a confirmed letter of credit. Use bank guarantees or standby letters of credit only with appropriate wording, collateral and authorized-bank review. Fedwire is a US domestic wholesale settlement system; the Spanish SL will normally access it through a US correspondent bank, regulated payment institution or treasury bank rather than directly. Maintain a payment matrix requiring dual approval, sanctions screening, invoice or contract support, segregation of duties, beneficiary verification, callback controls for changes to bank details and daily reconciliation. Avoid routing merchant funds through personal accounts or unrelated third-party accounts. For regulated payment activity, segregate and safeguard customer funds separately from corporate operating liquidity and document settlement timing, chargebacks, reserves and reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a regulated bank, supported by documented underlying exposure, approved counterparty limits, ISDA or bank master terms, valuation controls and accounting treatment.

Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency or jurisdiction does not permit practical delivery, subject to bank eligibility, local-law restrictions, documented commercial exposure and settlement through regulated counterparties.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented recurring funding or balance-sheet exposures, subject to EMIR-related reporting, clearing, margin, collateral and risk-management requirements where applicable.
Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity management and settlement-date mismatches, subject to treasury policy and counterparty limits.
Plain-vanilla currency options or collars for documented exposures, subject to suitability, premium, valuation, collateral and accounting controls.
Permitted euro and foreign-currency deposits or multicurrency accounts with regulated banks, with written limits on open positions and liquidity concentration.

The company should not use derivatives for unapproved speculation, should document the hedged item and risk objective, and should confirm that any payment-service, safeguarding, prudential, accounting and regulatory capital restrictions do not prohibit the proposed hedge.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and deposit of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual accounts must be approved within six months after the financial year-end and filed within one month after approval; for a 31 December year-end, filing is normally due by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure, financial penalties generally ranging from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, and potential administrative strike-off after one year of non-filing; directors may incur liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership declaration accompanying annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry and Central Beneficial Ownership Register mechanisms
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Beneficial ownership information must be confirmed or updated with the annual accounts filing and updated promptly after any ownership or control change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Filing rejection, registry closure, possible civil and administrative liability, and AML compliance deficiencies; inaccurate beneficial ownership information may trigger sanctions under Spanish AML legislation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period; for a calendar-year taxpayer, normally 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties generally apply as a fixed percentage of tax due, with surcharge rules for voluntary late filing; additional interest and penalties may apply where tax is unpaid or underreported.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT summary return, Modelo 390, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally filed from 1 to 30 January following the calendar year; taxpayers subject to the Immediate Supply of Information system may be exempt.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incorrect filing may result in fixed penalties, generally EUR 200 for a late informational return, subject to statutory reductions and exceptions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Related-party transactions information return, Modelo 232, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due in the eleventh month following the end of the tax period; for a 31 December year-end, normally 1 to 30 November.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Specific fixed penalties may apply for failure to file, late filing, or incomplete or inaccurate information; transfer-pricing adjustments and tax penalties may also arise.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual regulatory financial and governance reporting for a licensed payment institution or electronic money institution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Banco de España and other competent supervisory authorities, as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted according to the applicable Banco de España regulatory reporting calendar and authorization conditions; deadlines vary by reporting package and financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Supervisory remediation, infringement proceedings, monetary sanctions, restrictions on activity, and possible suspension or withdrawal of authorization.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is generally mandatory where the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets exceeding EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover exceeding EUR 5.7 million, or average employees exceeding 50. Audit is also mandatory in specified regulated, listed, grant-funded, consolidated, or sector-specific cases. A licensed payment institution or electronic money institution should be treated as potentially subject to sectoral audit requirements and Banco de España supervision.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the Spanish General Accounting Plan, with applicable sectoral rules for regulated payment businesses. IFRS applies where legally required, elected, or relevant to consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain has no separate annual shareholder confirmation filing for every company. The company must maintain an accurate shareholder register and update it after transfers. Beneficial ownership information must be confirmed or updated with the annual accounts filing and updated promptly when ownership or control changes. A licensed payment business must also maintain current ownership and qualifying-holding information for supervisory purposes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors and persons holding powers of representation
Minute Book containing shareholder and board resolutions
Register of contracts with the sole shareholder, if the company is unipersonal
Beneficial ownership records and supporting identification documentation
Accounting books and supporting accounting documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700-2,500 per year for registered-office, corporate secretarial, and filing-agent services; Spain has no general annual company-renewal fee.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000-12,000 for a non-complex SL; USD 12,000-35,000 or more for a licensed payment institution, cross-border group, regulated reporting environment, or complex transaction profile.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Super-deduction for R&D (100% or 200% in qualifying cases), innovation aid, and sector-specific reduced rates (e.g., 15% for certain digital or R&D activities)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 (Corporate Income Tax Return) via Agencia Tributaria Sede Electrónica
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 25 days after fiscal year-end (e.g., 25 January for calendar-year entities ending 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after adjustments, deductions, and incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For Spanish SL with foreign branches or permanent establishments, include attributable income; non-residents file Modelo 210 with Spanish WHT obligations

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 100-600 EUR per day of delay (max 6 months); additional 0.4% monthly interest on unpaid tax; criminal sanctions for fraudulent filings

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC application to Agencia Tributaria with beneficial ownership certificate, residency proof, and DTA documentation; approval typically within 1-3 months before payment
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 19% statutory (0-10% under most DTAs); Interest: 19% statutory (often 0% under treaties for related-party debt)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain's Law 11/2021 (ESR) requires demonstrable real economic activities, adequate employees, assets, and risks; non-compliance triggers recharacterization and penalties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or false deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty: imprisonment 6 months to 6 years, fines equal to 100% of evaded tax, plus restitution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, disqualification from corporate offices, and joint restitution obligations

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or file Local File/Master File documentation or apply arm's length principle
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines 5,000-50,000 EUR per violation; potential 100% adjustment of transfer prices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines and disqualification if willful misconduct

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without adequate local employees, premises, or decision-making substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of income, fines up to 1,000,000 EUR, and license suspension
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for fines and potential criminal sanctions for fraudulent substance claims

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement KYC/AML controls or report suspicious transactions in payment gateway operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 2,000,000 EUR, license revocation, and criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, travel bans, and disqualification

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold or remit Spanish WHT on dividends, royalties, or interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: WHT penalties 100% of unpaid tax plus 0.4% monthly interest; possible criminal evasion charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal restitution and disqualification from management
